metadata.scenario_context: Several large engineering firms are working together on a major construction project. They have planned to hold a crucial progress meeting in early December.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from South Korea agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose to keep the meeting on December 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discussion around finalizing the date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.message: Hmm... December 1st seems a bit early. What if we consider December 5th instead? It'll allow for more updates and a smoother discussion. I just feel like rushing might not be the best approach for such an important meeting.

shared_prefix.message: I understand why you'd think that, but December 1st still feels rushed to me. Maybe we can find a middle ground. As for discussing government actions, it would be nice if there was more openness, but the system here doesn’t allow for that. It's just the way things are...

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex, a 40-year-old male civil engineer from Japan.

shared_prefix.speaker: John, a 30-year-old male civil engineer from South Korea.
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our way, it's not about having more freedom; it's about the system we operate in. No, that's not how it works in South Korea. I think it's naive to think it should be any different.
